title: kv: hot-cold segmentation + cooperative background defrag to reduce fragmentation and spill events
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: memory fragmentation in the KV cache causes frequent small-page spillovers and elevated tail latency under mixed hot/cold workloads. This PR introduces a cooperative background defragmenter plus a hot/cold segmentation policy to reduce fragmentation, preemptively consolidate pages, and lower spill frequency. High-level changes: 1) hot/cold segmentation: newly-written and frequently-accessed keys are placed into a 'hot' arena while long-lived, infrequently-read entries are promoted to a 'cold' arena. Segmentation minimizes cross-allocation fragmentation and makes compaction targets predictable. 2) cooperative background defrag: an asynchronous defrag worker scans cold arenas and coalesces small free regions into large blocks using a relocation protocol that cooperates with the request executor (lightweight handoff of short-lived locks). The worker yields to latency-sensitive RPC handlers and registers progress via a defrag watermark to avoid repeat work. 3) integration with batch scheduler: the batch controller is defrag-aware — when the defrag watermark is high, we temporarily limit the maximum batch size and throttle batching growth so defrag-induced memory churn doesn't amplify tail latency. The controller resumes normal batching after defrag stabilizes. 4) preemptive spill path: when memory pressure crosses a configured soft threshold, the spill manager is invoked to write selected cold segments to the configured spill backend (local NVMe or S3) asynchronously; this is prioritized over evicting hot keys. 5) metrics and observability: new metrics (defrag_run_seconds_total, defrag_yield_count, defrag_relocated_bytes, hot_cold_ratio, preemptive_spill_events) and dashboards to correlate defrag activity with observed decreases in spill events and CPU usage. 6) tests and benchmarks: synthetic and integration tests covering relocation correctness, concurrent reads during relocation, and end-to-end load harnesses. Summary of impact (internal bench): under a mixed read-heavy + large-tail write workload with ~30% fragmentation, end-to-end p95 generation latency improved by 9--14% and spill events reduced by ~62%, while average CPU for defrag stayed < 6% of a single core. Design notes + compatibility: this is opt-in via runtime config flags (kv.hot_cold_enabled, kv.defrag_enabled, kv.defrag_cpu_limit, kv.spill_soft_threshold). Offline upgrade path included: nodes with older head won't be affected because hot/cold metadata is backward-compatible; coordinator performs a short rolling upgrade for metadata initialization. See docs/kv/defrag-design.md for detailed design, invariants, and failure modes.

review_conversation: Luca: Can the relocation protocol starve GC or long-running requests? Please add a fail-safe yield after N relocations.
Priya: Added yield_count and the worker yields after 512 relocations by default; made it configurable (kv.defrag_yield_limit).
Helen: Concerned about read consistency during relocation -- need RCU-style readers or short-lived locks.
Priya: Implemented relocation with short-lived move locks and atomic pointer swap; added a read-path check that falls back to slow-path if relocation observed.
Dmitri: Bench numbers look good but add a test for concurrent batch growth to ensure the batch scheduler backpressure avoids p99 regressions.
Priya: Added stress test with dynamic batch growth; CI benchmark job included and green locally.
release_notes:
- Introduces hot/cold KV segmentation to reduce fragmentation and optimize eviction decisions.
- Adds cooperative background defragmenter that coalesces free regions while yielding to latency-sensitive work.
- Adds preemptive spill path for cold segments to reduce emergency spill evictions.
- New metrics and dashboards to observe defrag/eviction behavior.
Note: feature is opt-in via runtime flags; disabled by default for older clusters.
